title: Catalogue search, sorting and category filter
context: Shoppers search, sort and filter the tool catalogue. The web shop and the public catalogue API (used by the mobile app) must behave the same way. The catalogue is a shared, public sandbox: evaluation only reads it.

sourcesRead.contributes: context and parity requirement (L17), catalogue API endpoints, parameters and response envelope (L19), AC-1…AC-7 (L23-L29), category ids from GET /categories/tree (L33), out of scope (L34). No attachments.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Searching the web shop for a term shows only products whose name contains the term, and a caption "Searched for: <term>".
acceptanceCriteria.quote: Searching the web shop for a term shows only products whose name contains the term, and a caption "Searched for: <term>".
acceptanceCriteria.entryPoint: web shop catalogue home page / — search box (G2)
outcomes: every product shown has a name that contains the term (letter case ignored, G7)

acceptanceCriteria.text: GET /products/search?q=<term> returns 200 with only products whose name contains the term, regardless of letter case (searching "PLIERS" finds the same products as "pliers").
acceptanceCriteria.quote: GET /products/search?q=<term> returns 200 with only products whose name contains the term, regardless of letter case (searching "PLIERS" finds the same products as "pliers").
outcomes: every product in data has a name that contains the term (letter case ignored)
searching "PLIERS" finds the same products as "pliers"

acceptanceCriteria.text: A search without matches shows "There are no products found." on the web shop, and the API returns 200 with an empty data list and total 0.

acceptanceCriteria.entryPoint: web shop catalogue home page / — search box (G2)
outcomes: web shop shows "There are no products found."

acceptanceCriteria.text: Filtering the web shop by the category "Hammer" shows only hammers; GET /products?by_category=<id of Hammer> returns only products in that category.
acceptanceCriteria.quote: Filtering the web shop by the category "Hammer" shows only hammers; GET /products?by_category=<id of Hammer> returns only products in that category.

acceptanceCriteria.text: An empty search (no term) returns all products, so the mobile app can reuse the search endpoint for its "All tools" screen.
acceptanceCriteria.quote: An empty search (no term) returns all products, so the mobile app can reuse the search endpoint for its "All tools" screen.
outcomes: a search with no term returns all products (total equals the total of the unfiltered catalogue list GET /products, G6)

endpoints.request: query: sort (e.g. price,asc), by_category (category id), page

endpoints.success: one product, including its category (id, name)

rules.text: GET /products and GET /products/search both return { current_page, data: [products], per_page, total, last_page }
GET /products lists products, takes sort and by_category parameters and is paginated; GET /products/search?q=<term> searches
The web shop and the public catalogue API must behave the same way

auth.mechanism: none: public catalogue API and public web shop (no sign-in needed)

testData.strategy: None created: every test only reads the existing catalogue. Search terms come from the story ("pliers" / "PLIERS"); the no-match search uses a random nonsense term unique to the run; the Hammer category id is looked up at run time from GET /categories/tree.
constraints: the catalogue is a shared sandbox: other users' data exists, so never hard-code product names, counts or totals
compare web shop and API (and search vs list totals) within the same run
read-only: nothing is created, updated or deleted
